title: Financial Accountant Salary: Hourly Rates, Awards, and Annual Pay in Australia
description: Understand the financial accountant salary in Australia. Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay, award coverage, tax, and superannuation using official sources.
salarySummary: The median full-time financial accountant salary is around $2,003 per week or $104,156 per year based on 38 hours, but award rates and the National Minimum Wage set a lower floor.

faqs.q: What is the typical financial accountant salary in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the median full-time earnings for accountants (including financial accountants) is $2,003 per week as of May 2025. This equates to about $104,156 per year for a 38-hour week. However, actual pay varies by experience, industry, and location. Entry-level roles may start near award rates, while senior positions can exceed the median.

faqs.q: Are financial accountants covered by an award?
faqs.a: It depends on the employer. Accountants working for an accounting firm are generally not covered by an award and are entitled only to the National Minimum Wage and National Employment Standards. If the employer is in an industry covered by an award (e.g., banking, coal mining, electrical power), the accountant may be covered by that award. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides detailed guidance on award coverage for accounts employees.

faqs.q: How do I convert a financial accountant hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross salary. For example, $50 per hour gives $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year. Remember that superannuation (12% from 1 July 2026) is paid on top of this amount, and tax is deducted based on the 2026–27 resident tax scales.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Financial Accountant Salary

When evaluating a **financial accountant salary** in Australia, it helps to start with the hourly rate and work up to the annual figure. Whether you are an employer setting a rate or an employee negotiating an offer, knowing how to convert between hourly, weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay ensures clarity. This article uses official data from the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office to give you a reliable picture.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard conversion for a full-time employee is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a typical 38-hour week, this becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your **financial accountant salary** is offered at $55 per hour, your annual gross would be $55 × 38 × 52 = $108,680. To find the fortnightly amount, multiply the weekly pay by 2: $55 × 38 = $2,090 per week, so $4,180 per fortnight.

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparison.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Ombudsman. This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

However, many **financial accountant** roles are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. For example, the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award may apply to accountants in that industry, while the Clerks Award could cover accounts clerks or bookkeepers. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) list the specific minimum rates for each classification.

### Award Coverage for Financial Accountants

The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that accountants working for an accounting firm are generally not covered by any award. They are entitled only to the National Minimum Wage and the National Employment Standards. But if you work as a financial accountant for a bank, a coal mine, or an electrical power company, you may be covered by the relevant industry award. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site provides further details on award-free employment.

For non-accountant accounts employees (e.g., payroll officers, accounts clerks), awards such as the Clerks Award or Retail Award may apply if the employer’s industry does not have its own clerical classifications. Always check the specific award using the Fair Work Ombudsman’s tools.

### Median Earnings from the ABS

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that the median full-time earnings for accountants (ANZSCO 2211) are $2,003 per week as of May 2025. This translates to about $104,156 per year for a 38-hour week. The median hourly rate is $53. These figures are higher than the National Minimum Wage and reflect the professional nature of the role. However, they are medians – half of accountants earn more, half earn less. Entry-level financial accountants may start closer to award rates, while experienced professionals can earn well above the median.

### Tax and Superannuation

Once you have your annual gross **financial accountant salary**, you need to consider tax and superannuation. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $100,000, your employer must contribute an additional $12,000 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra cost for the employer.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: if you are a casual employee, do not include the loading in your base rate – check the box and the tool adds it for you.

### Putting It All Together

A **financial accountant salary** can range from the National Minimum Wage (if award-free and entry-level) to well over $150,000 for senior roles in professional services. The median of $2,003 per week is a useful benchmark. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to get your annual figure, then apply tax and super to understand your take-home pay. For more detailed comparisons, refer to the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) pages.

Always verify your specific award or agreement with the Fair Work Ombudsman, and consult a tax professional for personalised advice. The figures here are estimates based on official sources and should not replace professional determination.
